title: Introduce budget-tiered profile curator and heuristic bundler for cost-aware defaults
author: Asha Raman
description:
Motivation: We need a lightweight, opinionated curator that generates cost-aware defaults for new deployments and suggests tiered profiles (budget/standard/premium) for batching, cache presize, and quantization level. This PR adds a heuristic bundler that composes small, explainable profile templates and a curator CLI that can scaffold and shadow-evaluate them against a sampled workload. Goals: 1) reduce time-to-safe-defaults for teams onboarding Dedicated/Private deployments; 2) provide measurable unit-econ deltas between tiers; 3) make profile suggestions auditable and reversible.

What this PR does: single-string summary of changes below. Implement a profile curator service (library + CLI) that: - generates tiered templates for batching+cache+quant (three budgets: low/medium/high) - adds an Orchestrator hook to run shadow evaluations and collect token-level cost deltas - ships a compact format for 'profile bundles' (YAML) that can be stored with model metadata - introduces a 'heuristic bundler' which assembles presets from simple rules (e.g. frequent short requests => aggressive batching + small cache; long-form completions => conservative batching + higher-precision quant) - surfaces an explainability payload (why X preset chosen) for auditability - wires up conservative rollout: newly generated defaults are suggested in the Console but not applied until accepted.

Testing & validation: - unit tests for bundler rules and profile serialization - integration test that runs the CLI scaffold against a synthetic workload and asserts cost, latency, and quality thresholds - shadow evaluation harness that runs candidate profiles against live traffic (sampled) and records token economics without affecting production flows - comparative evals against current defaults to produce delta report.

Rollback & safety: - Bundles are non-destructive; Console interaction required for activation. - All curated profiles include a safe-fallback mapping (model-variant + region) to prevent capacity regressions. - Added telemetry to detect quality regressions (prompt sets, BLEU-like metrics for targeted workloads) and automatic revert suggestion.

Upgrade notes: This PR introduces a new dependency (pyyaml-light) for parsing profile bundles in the curator CLI and a small runtime hook in the serving runtime for shadow evaluations. See release notes below.

Related work: ENG-8321 (profile curator epic), ENG-8390 (shadow eval infra).
commit_summary: feat(curator): add profile-bundler library and initial rule set
feat(cli): scaffold 'rw-curate' CLI and YAML bundle serializer
feat(shadow): add shadow-eval hook and lightweight recorder
test: add unit/integration tests for bundler and bundle roundtrip
docs: add curator README and Console proposal for opt-in defaults
review_comments: Liam Chen (review): Nice separation of concerns. A couple of questions on the heuristics: how do we prevent oscillation when traffic mixes short and long requests?

Asha Raman (author reply): We added a traffic-segmentation step in the bundler and prefer conservative defaults when segment weight < 0.2. Also the shadow eval produces a confidence score used by Console to downgrade the suggestion if low.
Priya Nair (review): Please add a unit test that ensures the YAML bundle roundtrips correctly for the full schema (including explainability payload).
Asha Raman (author): Added test_bundler::test_bundle_roundtrip in tests/curator. Also added a small JSON schema comment in profile_schema.yaml.
Diego Alvarez (review): CI failed once due to flakiness in the shadow recorder tests; can we stub timeouts to avoid intermittent network timings?
Asha Raman (author): Adjusted shadow recorder test to use a deterministic fake clock and re-ran CI; flakiness resolved.
release_notes: - New: profile curator service and 'rw-curate' CLI that generates budget-tiered profile bundles (low/medium/high). - New: shadow evaluation hook to measure token-level cost deltas for candidate profiles. - Change: Console can now surface curated default suggestions in the Defaults panel (opt-in). - Ops: added guidance for safe rollout in ops/deploy/README-curator.md.
